title: progressive-pressure-relief-and-regional-handoff
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce progressive pressure relief (soft per-route eviction and regional handoff); add `dampened-open` circuit state to reduce thrash; new runtime knobs: pressure_window_ms, handoff_fraction, dampen_backoff_ms; canary rollout to 5% of traffic; no API changes.
description:
Motivation: During a recent maintenance window we observed tightly-coupled bursts across regions that triggered rapid circuit flips and cascading failovers. The consequence was unpredictable latency spikes for low-priority routes and unnecessary cross-region failover churn. This hotfix implements a progressive pressure relief strategy and a safer regional handoff path to reduce thrash while preserving SLOs.

What this PR does (single-line sections for compatibility): Implements a progressive pressure relief controller in the serving scheduler that: (1) applies a soft, per-route eviction curve instead of immediate hard drops; (2) introduces ephemeral capacity leases to allow short warm-up windows; (3) provides a regional handoff path that moves low-priority traffic to a neighboring region with backoff and telemetry; (4) adds a new circuit state `dampened-open` that waits an exponential dampen_backoff_ms before re-evaluating reopen; (5) exposes three runtime knobs: pressure_window_ms, handoff_fraction, dampen_backoff_ms for safe tuning.

Files changed: scheduler core, circuit state machine, config schema, unit + integration tests, runtime docs, canary rollout script.

Why this is safe: changes are additive and guarded by feature flags. Default behavior remains unchanged until the feature flag is enabled. Canary rollout plan included.

Testing and rollout: unit tests for eviction curve and lease expiry added; integration test simulates cross-region burst and verifies reduced handoff rate and fewer circuit flips; metrics and tracing added for pressure_events, handoff_decisions, dampened_open_count. Canary ran for 48h at 5% traffic in eu-west-1 with no increase in error-rate and a 42% reduction in circuit reopen events.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc attached (ENG-8421) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Canary script and dashboard queries - [x] Feature flag gating and default off - [x] Backwards-compatible config changes - [x] Ops runbook update (brief note in docs)

Rollout plan: 1) merge to main behind feature flag; 2) enable 5% canary in eu-west-1 for 24-48h; 3) monitor pressure_events, handoff_decisions, p95 latency for affected routes; 4) scale canary gradually to 25% and then 100% if stable.

Related: SUP-4123 (incident), ENG-8421 (design), follow-up task: ENG-8622 to add tenancy-aware handoff budgeting.
